REPORT OF THE WOMEN'S WING:

Mrs. Mngusuur Ager presented the report of the Women's Wing. She informed the board that the wing had organised a soap-making training session for 25 women from the surrounding villages on the 7th and 8th of March 2026. The training was facilitated by Mrs. Grace Ujah, a chemist from Makurdi. The participants had each paid a registration fee of ₦500, and the total amount realised was ₦12,500. The wing had spent ₦8,700 on caustic soda, palm oil, and other materials, leaving a balance of ₦3,800 which had been remitted to the Treasurer.

The Women's Wing also proposed that a similar training be organised for the production of groundnut oil, as many members had expressed interest. The board welcomed the proposal and asked the Women's Wing to prepare a detailed budget for consideration at the next meeting.

COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS:

The board reviewed the various committees of the cooperative and confirmed the following assignments for the remainder of the year:

1. Disciplinary Committee: Mr. Iorwase Aernan (Chairman), Mr. Dooior Hembe, Mrs. Mngusuur Ager.
2. Produce Marketing Committee: Mr. Aondoaver Akaangee (Chairman), Mr. Terkula Ikyo, Mrs. Ngozi Okafor.
3. Welfare Committee: Mrs. Mngusuur Ager (Chairman), Miss Terhemen Akaangee, Mr. Iorwase Aernan.
4. Audit Committee: Mr. Terkula Ikyo (Chairman), Mrs. Ngozi Okafor, Mr. Dooior Hembe.

The Chairman reminded the committees that they were expected to submit a brief report of their activities at each monthly board meeting.

MEMBER GRIEVANCES:

Adaeze Okafor official_role is Secretary. Record status: current.

The board considered a complaint brought by Mr. Aondofan Aernan, a member of the cooperative, regarding the sharing of the proceeds from the sale of the 2025 groundnut harvest. Mr. Aernan claimed that his share had been calculated incorrectly, as he had delivered 12 bags of unshelled groundnuts but had been paid for only 11. The Secretary was directed to check the produce receipt book for the relevant date and to report back to the board at the next meeting.

A second grievance was raised concerning the condition of the cooperative's store in Ushongo town. A member, Mrs. Atser Akaangee, reported that the roof of the store had been leaking during the last rains, and that some bags of maize had been damaged. The Chairman stated that he had inspected the store on the 12th of March and confirmed that the damage was limited to five bags. The board resolved that the roof should be repaired as a matter of urgency, and the Treasurer was directed to release funds for the purchase of zinc sheets and nails.

ACTION: Treasurer to release funds for the repair of the cooperative store roof.

TRAINING SCHEDULE:

The board discussed the training needs of members for the coming planting season. It was agreed that a one-day training on the application of fertiliser and the control of fall armyworm would be organised for members in April 2026. The training would be conducted by an extension agent from the Benue State Agricultural Development Programme. The date would be communicated to members through the village announcers and by notices posted at the cooperative's office and at the central market.

The board also noted that the two members nominated to attend the BSADP workshop on improved storage techniques, Mrs. Ngozi Okafor and Mr. Iorwase Aernan, were expected to give a report of the workshop at the next general meeting. The Chairman urged them to take detailed notes so that the knowledge could be shared with the wider membership.

ANY OTHER BUSINESS:

The Chairman informed the board that the cooperative had been invited to participate in the annual Ushongo Local Government Agricultural Show, which was scheduled to hold on the 18th of April 2026. The board resolved that the cooperative would participate and that a stand would be erected to display the cooperative's produce, including yams, maize, and cassava flour. The Produce Marketing Committee was directed to make the necessary arrangements.

2. READING AND ADOPTION OF MINUTES
The minutes of the previous board meeting, held on 2nd March 2026, were read by the Secretary. The Chairman asked if there were any corrections. Mr. Iyortyom observed that the minutes recorded that the training on improved storage techniques would be held in May, but he recalled that the date had been moved forward to the last week of April. The Secretary confirmed that the change had been communicated verbally after the meeting and that the minutes should reflect the new date. The minutes were corrected accordingly.

The minutes, as corrected, were adopted on a motion by Mrs. Okafor, seconded by Mr. Aernan.

3. MATTERS ARISING FROM THE MINUTES
a) Repair of the Cooperative Store Roof
The Chairman reported that the Treasurer, Mr. Tunde Bakare, had released funds for the purchase of zinc sheets and nails on the 20th of March. The roofing work was carried out by two members, Mr. Atser and Mr. Udam, over three days, and was completed on the 28th of March. The Chairman had inspected the work and confirmed that the roof was now sound. The total cost of materials was ₦18,500, and the labour was provided free of charge by the two members. The board thanked Mr. Atser and Mr. Udam for their contribution.

b) BSADP Workshop on Improved Storage Techniques
Mrs. Okafor and Mr. Aernan reported that they had attended the workshop, which was held in Makurdi on the 25th and 26th of March. They said that the workshop covered the construction of raised platforms for storing grain, the use of hermetic bags, and the proper treatment of maize before storage. They had taken detailed notes and would present a full report at the next general meeting. The Chairman thanked them and reminded them to include practical photographs if possible.

c) Training on Fertiliser Application and Fall Armyworm Control
The Chairman noted that the training, which had been discussed at the previous meeting, was still to be scheduled. He invited Mr. Hwande, the extension agent present, to speak to this item.

Mr. Hwande addressed the board. He said that the training would be most effective if held before the main planting, which was expected to begin in the third week of April. He proposed Saturday, 18th April 2026, as a suitable date, as most members would not be working in the fields that day. He also noted that the annual Ushongo Local Government Agricultural Show was scheduled for the same day, and asked whether there would be a conflict. After discussion, the board agreed that the training would be held on the 18th of April, and that the cooperative's stand at the Agricultural Show would be manned by a separate team drawn from the Produce Marketing Committee, so that members could attend the training without neglecting the show.

4. FINANCIAL REPORT
The Treasurer, Mr. Tunde Bakare, presented the financial report for the month of March 2026. He stated that the cooperative's total income for the month was ₦142,300, comprising:
- Sales of maize from the store: ₦96,800
- Sales of cassava flour: ₦21,500
- Membership dues: ₦9,000
- Interest on the cooperative's savings account: ₦2,000
- Other income (sale of empty bags): ₦3,000

Total expenditure for the month was ₦87,650, as follows:
- Purchase of zinc sheets and nails for store roof: ₦18,500
- Transport of maize to Makurdi market: ₦12,000
- Purchase of 10 empty bags for storage: ₦2,500
- Payment to Mr. Hwande for the March training on soil testing: ₦5,000
- Fuel for the cooperative's motorcycle: ₦4,000
- Stationery and printing of receipts: ₦1,650
- Repayment of loan from the microfinance bank: ₦30,000
- Miscellaneous (brooms, kerosene for the office lamp): ₦2,000
- Contribution to the Ushongo Local Government Agricultural Show registration fee: ₦12,000

The Treasurer reported a closing cash balance of ₦54,650 as at 31st March 2026, and a savings account balance of ₦210,000.

**6. LAND ALLOCATION AND FARM PREPARATION**

The Vice-Chairman, Mr. Simon Aondona, who also serves as the chairman of the Land Allocation Committee, reported on the status of land preparation for the season. He informed the board that the cooperative's group farm at Tse-Agberagba, comprising approximately 12 hectares, had been surveyed and marked out in March. The farm had been divided into plots as follows:

- Plot A (3.5 ha): Maize, for the cooperative's collective harvest
- Plot B (2.5 ha): Cassava, for members who requested land
- Plot C (2.0 ha): Groundnut, for members who requested land
- Plot D (2.0 ha): Vegetables (tomato, pepper, okra), for the cooperative's market garden
- Plot E (2.0 ha): Reserved for late applicants and for the children's school garden project

Mr. Aondona reported that the bush clearing on Plots A and C had been completed during the last week of March, using hired labour at a cost of ₦8,500. He noted that the clearing of Plot B had been delayed because of the late harvest of the previous cassava crop on that plot. The remaining plots were still to be cleared.

He also reported that the cooperative's two tractors—the Massey Ferguson and the smaller Ford—had both been serviced in March. The Massey Ferguson was in good condition, but the Ford had developed a fault in its hydraulic system and would require a replacement part. The mechanic, Mr. James Ugbede, had been asked to source the part from Makurdi, and the estimated cost was ₦15,000. The board agreed to approve this expenditure.

**ACTION: Land Allocation Committee to complete the clearing of Plots B, D, and E on or before 20th April 2026, using hired labour where necessary.**

**ACTION: Treasurer to pay Mr. Ugbede the sum of ₦15,000 for the replacement part for the Ford tractor upon presentation of a receipt.**

The Treasurer, Mr. John Adikwu, confirmed that the sum of ₦15,000 had been set aside for this purpose. The board agreed that the payment would be made to Mr. Ugbede upon presentation of a receipt, as previously resolved.

Mrs. Nyitar proposed that the training be held on Saturday, 18th April 2026, at the cooperative hall. The training would cover the following topics:

**1. OPENING AND PRAYER**

The meeting was called to order at 10:15 a.m. by the Chairman, Mr. Terlumun Akaa. He welcomed all members present and noted that this was the first board meeting since the training session of 18th April. The opening prayer was offered by Mr. Aondofa Iorliam.

**2. READING AND ADOPTION OF MINUTES OF THE PREVIOUS MEETING**

The minutes of the meeting held on 25th March 2026 were read by the Secretary. The minutes were adopted as a true record of the proceedings, subject to the following correction:

- In Item 7, the amount approved for the purchase of maize seeds should read ₦86,500 and not ₦86,000 as recorded. The Treasurer confirmed that the correct amount was approved and that the payment voucher reflects this figure.

The minutes were then signed by the Chairman and the Secretary.

**3. MATTERS ARISING**

**3.1 Repair of the Ford Tractor**

Mr. Iorwa Ugbede reported that the replacement part for the Ford tractor had been purchased and fitted. He stated that the tractor was now in good working condition and had been used for ploughing on the group farm for two days. The Chairman thanked Mr. Ugbede for completing the repair before the deadline of 12th April 2026.

The Treasurer reported that payment of ₦15,000 had been made to Mr. Ugbede upon presentation of the receipt, as resolved at the previous meeting.

**3.2 Clearing of the Group Farm**

The Chairman reported that the clearing of the group farm was completed on 20th April 2026 as scheduled. The hired labourers were paid in full. A total of 12.5 hectares was cleared. Members present expressed satisfaction with the quality of the clearing work.

**3.3 Fertilizer Distribution**

The Chairman reported that the fertilizer distribution exercise was completed successfully. A total of 120 bags of NPK 15-15-15 and 80 bags of urea were distributed to members. The distribution was done on a first-come, first-served basis as agreed. The Chairman noted that a few members had complained about the quality of the fertilizer, but the matter was referred to the ADP for verification.

**4. ADDRESS BY MR. TERHEMBA HEMBA, ADP EXTENSION OFFICER**

Mr. Terhemba Hemba, the ADP Extension Officer, was invited by the Chairman to address the board. Mr. Hemba thanked the cooperative for the invitation to the training session held on 18th April 2026. He noted that participation was good, with over 60 members and family members attending.

Mr. Hemba then gave a brief update on the current planting season:

- The rains have been irregular so far. Farmers who planted early maize in April may need to replant in some areas where germination was poor.
- He advised that cassava cuttings should be planted as soon as possible, as the late rains would still support establishment.
- He recommended that members use the compost and organic manure as taught during the training, as chemical fertilizer prices remain high.

Mr. Hemba also informed the board that the ADP would be conducting a follow-up visit to the cooperative's group farm in the first week of May to assess the progress of the maize crop and to provide technical advice on weed control.

The Chairman thanked Mr. Hemba for his continued support and for the useful advice.

**ACTION: Secretary to write a letter of appreciation to the ADP office, to be signed by the Chairman.**
